title: How far does she walk, and who goes round the park faster?
description: Two problems use taking away fractions. The first finds the rest of a distance after an auto ride. The second compares two times for going round a park and finds how much quicker one is.
teaching_notes: One idea: a story about the rest, or about how much more or less, is a take away of fractions. Change both fractions to the same bottom number, take away the tops and keep the bottom. Watch for students who compare ten thirds and thirteen fourths by their tops alone.

source: Solve the following problems: a) Jaya's school is 7/10 km from her home. She takes an auto for 1/2 km from her home daily, and then walks the remaining distance to reach her school. How much does she walk daily to reach the school? b) Jeevika takes 10/3 minutes to take a complete round of the park and her friend Namit takes 13/4 minutes to do the same. Who takes less time and by how much?
video_script.why: The child turns two word problems into taking away fractions, changes each pair to the same bottom number, and takes away the tops, the way the book's solved question does.
video_script.substitution: The book's method for taking away fractions with different bottom numbers, used on a walk to school and on two times round a park.
video_script.anchor: two short problems written side by side on the board: a walk to school and two times round the park, as in the book
video_script.payoff_line: The walk is one fifth of a kilometre, and Jia is quicker by one twelfth of a minute

final_answer.value: 1/5 km; Jia is quicker by 1/12 minute
final_answer.spoken: the walk is one fifth of a kilometre, and Jia is quicker by one twelfth of a minute

video_script.fraction_reading: seven tenths, one half, five tenths, two tenths, one fifth, ten thirds, thirteen fourths, forty twelfths, thirty nine twelfths, one twelfth

names.Ziva: goes round the park in ten thirds of a minute
names.Jia: goes round the park in thirteen fourths of a minute

hold_back: 1/5 km; Jia is quicker by 1/12 minute
never_show: the two answers together in one line before the answer beat
maths_rules: 39/12 is less than 40/12, so Jia takes less time
ground demo: a trip of 5/6 km with 2/6 by auto leaves 3/6 to walk
video_script.design: One idea: the rest and how much quicker are taking away fractions. The two problems stay on the board as the anchor and each step works on one of them in order.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, with two problems to solve.
<bookmark mark='first'/>In the first, a child lives seven tenths of a kilometre from school. She takes an auto for one half of a kilometre, then walks the rest.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In the second, Ziva takes ten thirds of a minute to go round the park. Jia takes thirteen fourths of a minute.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How far does the child walk? Who takes less time, and by how much?

beats.on_screen: the road and the park hold still and the questions stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a strip cut into 6 equal parts with 5 shaded as a trip; 2 shaded parts marked auto and 3 parts marked walk; below it the words same bottom number, then compare the tops

marks.rest: the words the rest = the whole trip − the part covered appear
marks.strip: a strip of 6 equal parts appears with 5 shaded, 2 marked auto and 3 marked walk
marks.compare: the words same bottom number, then compare the tops appear

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>To find the rest of a distance, we take away the part already covered.
<bookmark mark='strip'/>Here a trip of five sixths of a kilometre is drawn as a strip. Two sixths go by auto, and three sixths are left to walk.
<bookmark mark='compare'/>To find which of two fractions is smaller, use the same bottom number. Then compare the tops.

beats.on_screen: Given: school 7/10 km away; auto 1/2 km; Ziva takes 10/3 minutes; Jia takes 13/4 minutes

marks.given: the distances are written on the working board
marks.park: the two times are written beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the school is seven tenths of a kilometre away. The auto goes one half of a kilometre.
<bookmark mark='park'/>Ziva takes ten thirds of a minute, and Jia takes thirteen fourths of a minute.

beats.on_screen: To find: the distance walked; who takes less time, and by how much

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the distance the child walks, and who takes less time.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: walk = whole distance − auto distance = 7/10 − 1/2 km

marks.rest: the words walk = whole distance − auto distance are written
marks.write: 7/10 − 1/2 is written with the unit km

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step one, the child walks the rest of the way. The rest is the whole distance take away the auto distance.
<bookmark mark='write'/>We write seven tenths take away one half, in kilometres.

marks.mult: the top 1 and the bottom 2 are each multiplied by 5 and 5/10 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='bottom'/>Step two, tenths and halves need the same bottom number. Two times five is ten, so change the half into tenths.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Multiply the top and the bottom of one half by five. That gives five tenths.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Seven take away five is two, so we get two tenths.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Two and ten both divide by two, which gives one fifth of a kilometre.

marks.less: 39/12 < 40/12 is written and Jia's time glows

narration: <bookmark mark='twelve'/>Step three, to see who takes less time, change thirds and fourths to twelfths. Three times four is twelve.
<bookmark mark='conv'/>Ten thirds becomes forty twelfths, and thirteen fourths becomes thirty nine twelfths.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Thirty nine is less than forty, so Jia takes less time.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Step four, the time Jia saves is forty twelfths take away thirty nine twelfths.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Forty take away thirty nine is one, so the time saved is one twelfth of a minute.

marks.back: each answer slides back beside the part that was taken away

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step five, check by putting each answer back in its question.
<bookmark mark='walk'/>Two tenths for the walk and five tenths for the auto make seven tenths. That is the whole distance.
<bookmark mark='time'/>Thirty nine twelfths and one twelfth make forty twelfths, the longer time.

beats.on_screen: Answers: the walk is 1/5 km; Jia is quicker by 1/12 minute

marks.ans: the two answers 1/5 km and 1/12 minute are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The walk is one fifth of a kilometre, and Jia is quicker by one twelfth of a minute.
